How long do pedkindraw's computations and drawings take, and how large a
pedigree can each one handle? This vignette answers from timing studies run
in November 2026 on one machine. pedkindraw did not time itself: most of its
code is copied from nprcgenekeepr, and the studies timed nprcgenekeepr's code
beside kinship2 and Pedixplorer. Each table says which code it timed and
when, and the second section says why that code stands for pedkindraw's.
Every number in the tables was checked against the studies' committed result
files by a script, `tools/checkSpeedTables.R` in pedkindraw's GitHub
repository. This page has no drawing and runs no code.

## The machine and the method

Every time comes from one machine: an Apple M2 Max with 12 cores and 96 GiB of
memory, running macOS and R 4.6.2. The packages compared were kinship2 1.9.6.2
and Pedixplorer 1.8.0.

Each run was a fresh R process. It loaded only the package being timed (and
Matrix), built its input before the clock started, and timed one call. A step
a user must run first was inside the timed call: pedkindraw's `kinship()` time
includes `findGeneration()`, and kinship2's kinship by family includes
`makefamid()`. For each computation and size, smallest first, a warm-up run
came first, which was also the test of whether that size fits; then three
measured runs, and the figure is their median. A run failed when it passed
120 seconds from the call's start or 32 GB of memory, and the sizes after a
computation's first failure were not run. Each run started only when at least
half of the CPU was idle (for the Rewrite record, at least 80% idle and half
the memory free).

The pedigrees are synthetic colonies of 300 to 100,000 animals, made by one
seeded generator that grows a colony a year at a time, and, for the drawings,
the 375-animal example pedigree that comes with pedkindraw
(`system.file("extdata", "obfuscated_rhesus_mhc_ped.csv", package =
"pedkindraw")`). Shrinking and the unrelated set use a seeded 30% of the
animals as genotyped (available) and 10% as affected; trimming to ancestors
or descendants starts from 5 seeded probands.

## Why these times stand for pedkindraw's

pedkindraw's copied code is nprcgenekeepr's at commit `baef1e12c`, except
`drawPedigreeDiagram.R`, copied at the later `4283e3502`. This table compares,
file by file, the code each study timed with the code pedkindraw copied:

<!-- speed-table: code -->

| Record | nprcgenekeepr code timed | Of the 34 copied files, those that differ |
|---|---|---|
| Part A | `70e0492eb` | `comparePedigreeStructure.R`, `drawPedigreeDiagram.R`, `kinship.R`, `makePedigreeDiagramData.R`, `mzTwinGroups.R`, `shrinkPedigree.R` |
| Part B | `fd7c3d8ce` | `comparePedigreeStructure.R`, `drawPedigreeDiagram.R`, `kinship.R`, `makePedigreeDiagramData.R`, `mzTwinGroups.R`, `shrinkPedigree.R` |
| Rewrite | `d280dc8e8` | `drawPedigreeDiagram.R` |

Table: Each copied file's nprcgenekeepr source at the code a record timed, compared by git with its source at the commit pedkindraw copied.

- Part A timed nprcgenekeepr before it rewrote its kinship and shrinking code
  (`kinship.R`, `mzTwinGroups.R` and `shrinkPedigree.R`) without code derived
  from kinship2. The other computations it timed (generation depth, family
  trees, ancestors and descendants) reach none of the files that differ, so
  their rows below are Part A's. The kinship and shrinking rows come from the
  Rewrite record, which timed the rewritten code: there only
  `drawPedigreeDiagram.R` differs, and that record timed no drawing.
- Part B timed the drawing before the rewrite of the layout's solver, in
  `makePedigreeDiagramData.R`. The Rewrite record timed the rewritten layout
  on one pedigree (the section "The rewrite" below); the drawing rows are
  Part B's.
- `drawPedigreeDiagram.R` also carries nprcgenekeepr's later changes to the
  legend and to the check of `onClick`, and `comparePedigreeStructure.R` is
  used only by tests.
- Since the copy, pedkindraw has added layout hints to three of the layout's
  functions and drawn each condition's legend row as a picture of its
  sections (`DIVERGENCE.md` in pedkindraw's repository). Given no hints, its
  layouts are the same as nprcgenekeepr's (`tools/compareResultsWithNprcgenekeepr.R`
  compares them). Neither change was timed.

## Computation

What each computation is, with the pedkindraw function that does it:

- **Kinship, autosomal**: `kinship()` gives the kinship coefficient of every
  pair of animals, the chance that a gene drawn at random from each of the
  two is the same copy inherited from a common ancestor, as a matrix with a
  row and a column for each animal.
- **Kinship, sparse**: `kinship(sparse = TRUE)` gives the same values as a
  sparse matrix, which stores only the pairs above 0. kinship2's nearest is
  its kinship within each family, `makekinship()`; Pedixplorer has none.
- **Kinship, X chromosome**: `kinship(chrtype = "x", sex = )` gives the
  kinship of genes on the X chromosome, which needs each animal's sex.
- **Generation depth**: `findGeneration()` numbers each animal's generation:
  0 for a founder (both parents unknown), and otherwise one more than the later
  of its known parents. A drawing puts the animals in rows by it, and
  `kinship()` needs it first.
- **Family trees**: `findPedigreeNumber()` gives each animal a family number,
  shared by every animal linked to it through sires, dams and offspring; an
  animal with no relative in the pedigree is a family of its own.
- **Shrink to 16 bits**: `shrinkPedigree()` removes animals until the
  pedigree's bit size is 16 or less, keeping the genotyped and affected
  animals that carry the most information. The bit size, twice the number of
  animals with a known parent less the number of founders, is kinship2's
  measure of a pedigree's size for software that cannot handle a large one.
  Each step tries every animal that could go and removes the one that lowers
  the bit size most, so the time grows much faster than the pedigree.
- **Unrelated set**: as many genotyped animals as can be found of which no two
  are related, that is, share an ancestor or descend one from the other.
  pedkindraw's `findUnrelated()` is its own code, timed separately below; the
  table times kinship2's and Pedixplorer's.
- **Probands and their ancestors**: `trimPedigree()` keeps a chosen group of
  animals (the probands) and all of their ancestors, and drops the rest.
- **Probands and their descendants**: `getDescendantPedigree()` keeps the
  probands and all of their descendants.
- **Build a pedigree object**: kinship2's `pedigree()` and Pedixplorer's
  `Pedigree()` turn a table of animals into the object their other functions
  take. pedkindraw works on the data frame itself.

Table: Seconds, by the number of animals. Part A: 2026-11-02, nprcgenekeepr `70e0492eb`, kinship2 1.9.6.2 and Pedixplorer 1.8.0; Rewrite: 2026-11-09, nprcgenekeepr `d280dc8e8` against its 3.0.0 (`fa1f2849e`). Apple M2 Max, 12 cores, 96 GiB, R 4.6.2.

Each figure is the median of 3 measured runs, to three significant figures;
"<0.001" is under a millisecond. "memory": the run passed 32 GB (R's own
limit on its heap, or the watchdog on the process's memory); "time": it passed
120 seconds; an empty cell: not run, after a failure; "not run": the Rewrite
record did not try that size. pedkindraw's rows name the function a user calls;
kinship2's
and Pedixplorer's ran their own counterparts (the study's section 3 lists
them). kinship2's kinship by family, `makekinship()`, is block-sparse, the
nearest it has to pedkindraw's sparse kinship; Pedixplorer has none.

What this means for pedkindraw:

- Its kinship is as fast as kinship2's, and a dense kinship matrix of 30,000
  animals takes under half a minute. The Rewrite record did not try 100,000
  animals; Part A stopped the code before the rewrite there on memory, and the
  Rewrite record found that the rewrite uses the same memory as that code.
- `findPedigreeNumber()` is the one slow row. Its time grows about with the
  square of the number of animals (tripling them from 10,000 to 30,000 took
  about 9 times as long), where kinship2's and Pedixplorer's grow about in
  proportion: 12.9 seconds at 100,000 animals, against well under a second.
- `shrinkPedigree()` shrinks 3,000 animals in 92 seconds; kinship2 and
  Pedixplorer passed 120 seconds at 3,000 and 1,000 animals. The Rewrite
  record did not try 10,000, which is likely far past the limit, but untested.
- The unrelated set is pedkindraw's own `findUnrelated()`, which the studies
  did not time; see "pedkindraw's own functions" below.
- pedkindraw takes a data frame, so it has no pedigree object to build;
  kinship2's and Pedixplorer's functions need theirs first.

"Largest size within the limits": the largest size that finished within 120
seconds and 32 GB. "Process peak": the process's largest resident memory there
(`/usr/bin/time -l`). "R heap peak": the most R's heap held above its starting
point, read at its garbage collections. macOS's resident figure leaves out
compressed memory, so near the limit the two can disagree, as for the sparse
kinship at 30,000. Part A stopped the code before the rewrite there for passing
32 GB, yet the Rewrite record, whose runs each waited for half the memory to be
free, finished it with both versions. Why was not found; at that size whether a
run fits depends on the machine's state.

## The rewrite

The Rewrite record timed nprcgenekeepr's rewritten code (`d280dc8e8`, the code
pedkindraw copied) against its 3.0.0 release, which still held code derived
from kinship2. Both gave identical results. Kinship took the same time to
within a few percent at every size, so only shrinking and the layout are shown
here:

<!-- speed-table: rewrite -->

| Computation | Animals | Before the rewrite (s) | The rewrite (s) | Before (MiB) | The rewrite (MiB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shrink to 16 bits | 300 | 0.703 | 0.105 | 156 | 57 |
| Shrink to 16 bits | 1,000 | 20.5 | 3.69 | 291 | 101 |
| Shrink to 16 bits | 3,000 | time | 92 |  | 128 |
| Layout, direct edges | 708 (a trimmed example) | 3.4 | 3.32 | 258 | 244 |

Table: Seconds and memory, before and after the rewrite. Rewrite: 2026-11-09, nprcgenekeepr `d280dc8e8` against its 3.0.0 (`fa1f2849e`). Apple M2 Max, 12 cores, 96 GiB, R 4.6.2.

Seconds: the median of three measured runs; "time": past 120 seconds. MiB: the
call's memory, the process's peak resident memory less its memory just before
the call. The layout is `makePedigreeMatingLayout()` with direct edges on a
708-animal trim of nprcgenekeepr's example pedigree.

A picture is a file written by R; a web page was opened in Chrome, and its
time is R's and the browser's together. Each figure is the median of 3
measured runs. "time": R and the browser together passed 120 seconds;
"refused": the package stopped with an error. No drawing reached 3,000

with the layout's default, rectilinear edges; pedkindraw's is a copy of it

Pedixplorer refused the synthetic colonies with its parent alignment on, and
its own warning suggests turning it off (`align_parents = FALSE`); its plotly

The JavaScript heap is the page's heap in use once it had drawn: a reading at
one moment, not a peak, which varied from run to run. Can a reader use a
drawing that large? In Part B the drawings were judged by eye for the largest
size at which an animal can still be found by its id and its lines followed
to its parents. nprcgenekeepr's drawing, pedkindraw's source, was readable at
1,000 animals once zoomed in; at its fitted view it shows no ids. kinship2's
and Pedixplorer's drawings were not readable at any size drawn, not even 300.

pedkindraw's new code is not in the studies. Each of these figures was timed
on the same Mac by the pedkindraw session that wrote the function and recorded
in the project's plan as a single figure, not with the studies' method:

<!-- speed-table: single-runs -->

| Function | Animals | Seconds | Note | Session |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `checkPedigree()` | the same, with 5 cycles put in | 0.22 |  | S17, 2026-11-13 |
| `findUnrelated()` | 10,000 (the study's colony), 30% genotyped | 0.57 | kinship2 in the study's Part A: 6.53 s | S18, 2026-11-13 |

pedkindraw's other functions of its own, `familyCheck()`, `ibdMatrix()`,
`bitSize()`, `findUnavailable()`, `findAvailNonInform()`,
`findAvailAffected()` and the layout hints, have no recorded time.

## What these numbers cannot tell you

- Another machine's times: these are one Mac's.
- A smaller machine's limits: the runs were allowed 32 GB on a machine with
  96 GiB, and the kinship matrices of the largest sizes need most of that; on
  a machine with less memory they can stop at a smaller size.
- Another browser's drawing time: the browser's part was timed in Chrome.
- The cost of pedkindraw's changes since the copy, the layout hints and the
  legend's pictures, which were not timed.
- A real pedigree's times: the studies' pedigrees are synthetic colonies, and
  a real pedigree of the same size can take longer or shorter.

## Where next

`vignette("pedkindraw", package = "pedkindraw")` takes the 375-animal example
pedigree from its records to a drawing, and `vignette("drawing", package =
"pedkindraw")` shows what a drawing shows and how to change it. `?pedkindraw`
lists every function by what it does.
